## Built-In Trap IDs

- `self_agreement_bias`: Target and judge share a vendor; judge's biases overlap with the target, flattering same-vendor responses.
- `small_sample_kc4_power`: Dataset is small enough that Pearson KC-4 has no statistical power; correlation threshold becomes a random pass/fail.
- `variants_homogeneous`: System prompt variants are too similar; sensitivity on the system_prompt_variant axis will be artificially low.
- `rubric_weight_concentration`: A single rubric dimension carries the majority of the weight; judge noise on that one dimension dominates the fitness.
- `judge_budget_too_small`: Judge output budget is SMALL but rubric has many dimensions + gates; judge response may be truncated before scoring all axes.
- `empty_reference_with_strict_rubric`: Dataset items have no reference text while the rubric's dimension descriptions imply comparison to a ground truth.
- `no_held_out_slice`: User did not pass --test; walk-forward cannot run; ship decision has no generalisation evidence.
- `train_test_id_overlap`: Items appear in both train and test, or duplicate ids exist within either slice; KC-4 / per-item correlation reads on a leaked dataset are meaningless.
- `routed_provider_opaque_family`: Target or judge is named as a multi-vendor routing aggregator (OpenRouter / Together / Fireworks / Groq / Bedrock / etc.); the underlying served model's family is not visible to the self-agreement-bias check, so the bias signal is unreliable.
